A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original prompt-injection defense experiments, utility and timing measurements, robustness analyses, and response examples in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on closed-source models and comparisons with fine-tuned StruQ variants.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same shield-prompt formulation and four defenses: Ignore, Escape, Fakecom, and Fakecom-t. The new experiments apply existing defenses without introducing a new component or procedure.

E1.justification: Reported coverage remains direct injection on 208 AlpacaFarm samples and indirect injection and clean utility evaluation on the 2,000-sample QA dataset. The additional experiments expand victim-model and comparator configurations within the retained tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds StruQ-Naive and StruQ-Ignore against Ours-Ignore in Table 7, substantially extending comparison beyond training-free defenses. It removes Incontext from the direct, indirect, utility, template-aware attack, GCG, and timing comparisons. The other existing baselines remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4o-Latest evaluations, restricted to Ignore and Fakecom defenses because conversation templates cannot be changed. It also introduces separate Naive- and Ignore-based StruQ fine-tuning conditions and removes the no-attack ASR control. Existing sample counts and the clean-QA utility metric remain unchanged as reported.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds an analysis of StruQ generalization to attacks beyond its fine-tuning attack. It removes the ASR false-positive validation and v1 Table 6. The GCG transfer, template-aware attack, attack–defense relationship, and case-study analyses are retained; Figure 3 is relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Averages across attacks or methods remain descriptive summaries.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces every retained utility score: for example, the best Llama3 entry changes from Ours-Fakecom-t at 79.50% to Sandwich at 80.80%. V2 adds closed-source results and StruQ baseline results, while removing Incontext and no-attack ASR entries. Matched entries in the original attack-defense and timing tables remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation in Section 4.1 is unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the shortened empirical metric discussion introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: V2 substantially broadens the headline comparison claim: the abstract and contribution bullet remove the training-free restriction, and the introduction explicitly adds comparability to fine-tuning-based methods. The central attack-derived defense contribution and near-zero-ASR claim remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about suitability for stronger closed-source models and StruQ's limited generalization, explaining its Combined-attack success through overlap with Ignore training. It presents the unchanged GCG results more positively and removes the ASR misclassification and bias discussion. Section 7's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 removes Section 5.1's explicit arithmetic attack target and evaluation rationale, leaving a generic answer-detection description; the arithmetic example survives in the case study. Incontext's implementation description and prompt example disappear. Appendix A.2's hardware and generation settings, dataset-access statements, and promised code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Hurst et al. (2024) and Jiang et al. (2023), removes Wei et al. (2023), and positions the method directly against the already-cited StruQ. The dedicated related-work discussion otherwise remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the metric explanation, locally reorganizes Section 5.4, adjusts introductory claims, and abbreviates the unusually long Llama3 reference author list. Most prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 4 and 7, removes v1's validation table and Incontext illustration, and deletes Incontext rows from retained tables. Figure 3 moves from the main text to the appendix, and other displays are renumbered or repositioned. The established visual design largely persists.

improvement.justification: The closed-source and StruQ comparisons add useful evidence about applicability and competitiveness. However, v2 removes the explicit ASR recipe and reliability check, replaces utility scores without explaining their revision, and provides limited training and evaluation details for StruQ. These gains in breadth coexist with reduced validation and unresolved comparison details, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
